St Gwynog's Church, Aberhafesp, Montgomeryshire, Powys SY16 3HW

In memory of the R.A.F. (V.R.) Airmen who died when their Halifax Aircraft crashed at Glascoed, Bwlch-y-ffridd in this Parish on 23rd January 1944. Their bodies rested at Bwlch-y-ffridd Institute on the evening of the 23rd.

paragraphs.text: Halifax V DG358 of 1667 Heavy Conversion Unit took off from RAF Faldingworth on 23 January 1944 on a day cross-country navigation exercise. All nine men aboard were killed when it crashed in the parish of Aberhafesp, Montgomeryshire. IBCC records say the engine failed at about 20,000 feet over Wales and the aircraft descended into thick cloud, where severe icing made a wing fold and come off; the Halifax then struck its own tailplane and broke up in the air. Aviation Safety Network, quoting an accident form, gives a probable engine failure at 20,000 feet before a hailstorm, with the pilot descending into cloud that proved to be a storm.

Three of the dead are fully identified so far. Sergeant Ellis Robert Gawler, the flight engineer, was 27 and is buried at Canford Magna. Sergeant John William Gibb, the navigator, was 18 and is buried in Aberdeen. Flight Sergeant John Stanley Spriggs, the air bomber, was 31 and is buried at Chester (Blacon).

notes: IBCC began returning HTTP 429 after three pages, so Bennett, Clark, Fisher, Ramsay (IBCC spells Ramsay), Wareham and Wyatt are named from the stone only; their IBCC pages (loss ids 101683, 104212, 107675, 119296, 124424, 126104) still need reading for rank, role, age, service number and burial. Search snippets suggest Wareham was a Sgt air gunner aged 20. ASN (S4) was not opened: both the host and its cdn mirror failed, so its details come from a search-result summary only. The lightning version of the cause (also mentioned in snippets, e.g. a Find a Grave entry and a website quoting 'hail storm, icing, lightning as well as engine trouble') was not read at source and is not claimed. Crash site naming differs: Glascoed Farm (memorial), Cwm Farm, Bryn-y-Groes (ASN/IBCC snippets). Brian Poole's 1998 booklet 'Down in Aberhafesp' was mentioned in a snippet and not seen. Custodian not found: St Gwynog's Church holds the roll, but no source read names who cares for it. Glascoed Farm memorial not researched. The IWM capture's single photo (credit Bill Williams) is not listed because its URL is not under the permitted pattern check.
